purpose: D4 successor to D1/D2/D3: adds special-illustration/full-art composition language on top of the D3 anime-intensity level, since D3 (the strongest of D1-D3) still read as ordinary slice-of-life anime rather than an iconic collectible moment. Also deliberately reduces literal 'trading card'/'collectible card'/'card frame' phrasing after D1 produced a severe fake-TCG-UI defect from that framing. Each block REPLACES only global_style_v1.json's top-level `prompt` field for this test; global_text_policy, global_screen_policy, and global_negatives are reused unchanged from production so semantic/content-safety behavior is held constant.
prior_rounds: catalog/style_calibration_d_18_v1.json (D1/D2/D3, D3 strongest but still ordinary anime lifestyle, not special-illustration)

D4.label: Japanese Special Illustration / Collectible Moment
D4.description: Japanese commercial-anime rendering + premium special-illustration/full-art composition language + real-world hobby storytelling. Targets an iconic 'this is the moment' focal hierarchy rather than ordinary slice-of-life anime staging.
D4.prompt:
Create a premium full-art Japanese-inspired special illustration for a real-world hobby.

This must be unmistakably illustrated artwork, not photography.

The rendering language should feel like polished contemporary Japanese commercial anime illustration:
- clean confident linework
- refined cel shading
- soft painted gradients
- expressive faces
- bright, appealing eyes
- elegant stylized anatomy
- crisp silhouettes
- lively gestures
- rich but controlled color
- luminous highlights
- polished finish

However, do NOT compose this as an ordinary slice-of-life anime scene.

Do NOT simply show people casually doing the hobby in a normal environment.

Instead, compose the scene as an ICONIC SPECIAL-ILLUSTRATION MOMENT.

The image should feel like a rare full-art key visual:
- one unforgettable focal moment
- a strong hero subject or hero interaction
- dynamic composition
- visual flow toward the hobby action
- foreground elements that create depth and energy
- supporting background shapes that serve the main subject
- directional environmental movement
- clear visual rhythm
- memorable silhouette
- strong palette identity
- heightened emotional expression
- a sense of “this is the moment”

The central subject should dominate the composition.

Use strong focal hierarchy:

1. HERO MOMENT
2. hobby-defining action / object
3. supporting people or environment
4. small delightful detail

Do not give equal visual importance to every person or object in the scene.

Do not spread attention evenly across the entire image.

Avoid ordinary documentary composition.

Avoid “a room full of people all doing things.”

Instead, stage a single emotional or action peak.

Use Japanese anime linework, polished cel shading, expressive but mature character design, bright harmonious palette, clean character silhouettes, dynamic staging, subtle rim light, sparkling highlights, small glints, stylized steam / wind / dust / paper movement where appropriate, graphic color accents, lively perspective, mild perspective exaggeration, foreground framing elements, strong diagonal or circular visual flow when helpful.

These effects should create excitement and collectibility.

They must NOT turn the scene into magic or fantasy unless the hobby itself requires fantasy.

Default emotional direction: joyful, engaging, optimistic, energetic, curious, triumphant, excited, socially alive, inviting, aspirational.

Serious subjects may use: tension, fascination, determination, revelation, intellectual excitement - but should not become gloomy, depressing, muted, solemn, academically lifeless, or dark prestige-TV realism.

Prefer clean, colorful palettes, warm/cool contrast, saturated but controlled hues, visually memorable palette identity, luminous accents, and attractive color separation between hero and background.

Avoid beige lifestyle palettes, muddy brown-heavy grading, monochrome editorial restraint, Western cinematic desaturation, and corporate muted color schemes.

IMPORTANT - the artwork must be full-bleed and edge-to-edge.

Do NOT draw: card border, white border, rounded frame, decorative frame, printed-paper edge, faux card shell, TCG layout, title bar, stats box, logo badge, corner emblem, rarity symbol, or UI panel.

The application will add any card UI later. The generated image itself must be pure artwork.

Do NOT render: photography, stock photo, DSLR realism, movie still, photo bokeh, photographic skin pores, lens blur, Western magazine editorial art, flat corporate illustration, New Yorker-like restrained editorial illustration, Western concept art, gritty fantasy splash art, dark prestige-TV look, bland slice-of-life composition, static lineup composition, “everyone equally important” composition, generic AI-anime portrait, chibi, preschool cartoon, hypersexualized anime proportions, fan-service pose, excessive magic, fantasy weapons unrelated to the hobby, supernatural aura, card frame, trading-card UI, readable logo/title text, franchise characters, or recognizable franchise-specific motifs.

Semantic fidelity remains mandatory. Do not sacrifice hobby correctness to achieve style.
